events.what_changed: Original text: right to seek and receive asylum. The consolidated SINALEVI text has no amendment note on art. 31. It sets no duty to inform anyone about asylum before rejection or deportation.
events.passage: 8) Toda persona extranjera tiene derecho a buscar y recibir asilo en el territorio nacional, en razón de los convenios internacionales suscritos y ratificados por el país.

events.instrument: Ley General de Migración y Extranjería, Ley N.º 8764
events.what_changed: The rejection record must state the reasons and observe Const. art. 31. It contains no duty to advise about asylum. No amendment note appears in the consolidated text.
events.passage: un acta en la que se indiquen los motivos del rechazo, la autoridad policial y migratoria que determinó los supuestos y la indicación de que podrá impugnarse en la sede consular costarricense, y que tal impugnación no tendrá efecto suspensivo alguno.

events.instrument: Reglamento de Personas Refugiadas, Decreto Ejecutivo N.º 36831-G
events.what_changed: A claim may be referred by another authority or inferred, including for people who do not know they may be refugees. This is a duty to refer, not to advise. The consolidated text shows no amendment note; the 2022 and 2024 reforms touched arts. 14, 54, 58, 59 and a transitorio, not this article.
events.passage: La persona interesada puede ser referida por alguna otra autoridad, incluso inferirse cuando existan problemas de comunicación, barreras idiomáticas, culturales, personas en detención administrativa o judicial y casos de personas que desconozcan su posible condición de persona refugiada.

events.instrument: Reglamento de Personas Refugiadas, Decreto Ejecutivo N.º 36831-G
events.what_changed: An official who learns, in writing or orally, that a person wishes to seek refugee status must ensure non-refoulement and notify the Refugee Unit. The duty arises only once the wish is expressed. No amendment note.
events.passage: Las autoridades, judiciales, administrativas, o cualquier otro funcionario habilitado que conozca mediante escrito o verbalmente del deseo de una persona extranjera de acceder al procedimiento para el reconocimiento de la condición de persona refugiada, es responsable de garantizar el respeto al principio de no devolución

events.article: Reglamento de Personas Refugiadas art. 14 (not a cited article)
events.what_changed: Restored the rule that asylum seekers have protection against return and the same guarantees as recognised refugees. It does not touch arts. 123, 124, 127 or 134 and creates no duty to inform before expulsion.
events.passage: la persona solicitante gozará de protección contra una devolución y de las mismas garantías que una persona refugiada reconocida, hasta tanto no se haya resuelto su solicitud. (Así reformado por el artículo 1° del decreto ejecutivo N° 44501 del 28 de mayo del 2024)

answers.repealed_search: I checked the SINALEVI consolidated texts of Ley 8764 and Decreto 36831-G for amendment notes ('Así reformado', 'Así adicionado', 'Derogado') on the cited articles. None appear on arts. 31, 64 or 65 of the Law or on arts. 123, 124, 127 or 134 of the Regulation. The Regulation's amendments (43810 of 2022, 44501 of 2024) touched arts. 14, 54, 58, 59 and a transitorio. So no duty to advise existed in 2020 and was later removed. I did not read the repealed predecessor law (Ley 8487 of 2005); it was replaced in 2010, well before 2020, so it has no bearing on 1 January 2020.

rulings.later: Not checked in this session. The starting coder lists Votos 2025-022749, 2025-027425 and 2026-037342 as citing it, unread.

answers.implementation_2020_evidence: Not rated, because there was no protection in 2020. For the record: according to the DGME's own reply to the Global Detention Project in July 2020, asylum could be requested at border posts during the COVID closure and Refugee Unit staff were sent once a person stated the wish to apply. That describes referral, not proactive advice. The US State Department's 2019 and 2020 reports describe a functioning but backlogged asylum system and say nothing about advising people before removal.

answers.sourcing_note: I dated the history from the SINALEVI consolidated texts, which note each amendment inline; the cited articles carry no notes, so the 2020 text matches today's. The 'versión original' view of Ley 8764 would not load, and the 2025 Sala ruling was not re-read in this session; it postdates 2020 anyway.

events.instrument: Ley General de Migración y Extranjería, Ley N.º 8764
events.what_changed: Direct non-refoulement to any country, of origin or not, where the asylum seeker's or refugee's life is at risk. It does not address onward (chain) refoulement. No amendment note.
events.passage: 9) Ningún extranjero solicitante de refugio o que se le haya otorgado dicha condición, podrá ser expulsado, deportado o rechazado a otro país, sea o no de origen, donde su derecho a la vida esté en riesgo.

events.instrument: Ley General de Migración y Extranjería, Ley N.º 8764
events.what_changed: Deportation may go to the country of origin or any third country that admits the person, with no check on onward protection. No amendment note.
events.passage: ARTÍCULO 184.- En los casos citados, la Dirección General ordenará la deportación de la persona extranjera a su país de origen o a un tercer país que lo admita.

events.instrument: Reglamento de Personas Refugiadas, Decreto Ejecutivo N.º 36831-G
events.what_changed: Bars expelling or returning a refugee or pending applicant to a country where their life, safety or freedom is in danger. It is a direct rule only. No amendment note.
events.passage: Ninguna persona refugiada o solicitante de esta condición pendiente de resolución firme e inapelable, podrá ser expulsado o devuelto al territorio de un país donde su vida, seguridad o libertad peligre por causa de su raza, religión, nacionalidad, género, pertenencia a determinado grupo social o de sus opiniones políticas.

answers.repealed_search: I searched the SINALEVI consolidated Ley 8764 and Decreto 36831-G for amendment or repeal notes on arts. 31, 64 and 184 of the Law and arts. 39 and 40 of the Regulation and found none. The Regulation's 2022 and 2024 amendments touched other articles (14, 54, 58, 59, transitorio). No chain-refoulement clause was found in any version. I did not read the earlier Ley 8487; it was replaced in 2010, before the date in question.
answers.implementation_2020_evidence: Not rated, because there was no specific protection. For context: in July 2020 the DGME reported that deportations continued only by land, to Nicaragua and Panama, and that removals to other countries were suspended (GDP survey). The chain-deportation criticisms date from 2025 and concern US deportees.

practice_sources.title: Costa Rica: Covid-19 and Detention (Global Detention Project, 27 July 2020)

answers.sourcing_note: The cited statutory and regulatory articles have no amendment notes in SINALEVI, so the 2020 text matches today's. I did not re-read Constitution art. 31 in this session; it has been in place since 1949 and is cited only as a direct-refoulement rule.

answers.implementation_2020_evidence: Around 2020 deportations ran through the DGME's ordinary individual procedure. In its July 2020 survey reply to the Global Detention Project, the DGME said deportations continued under Ley 8764, by land to Nicaragua and Panama only, and that apprehension was ordered on an individual risk basis. The US State Department's 2019 report says the government generally observed the constitutional bar on arbitrary detention, and that the Heredia migration facility held irregular migrants until deportation or regularisation, with UNHCR visiting monthly. I found no documented pattern of collective removals without individual decisions for 2019–2020; the major documented breach (US deportees held at CATEM without individual resolutions) dates from 2025. The evidence is thin and partly the government's own account, so confidence is limited.

answers.implementation_2020_evidence: The structural limits were the same in 2020: deportation was a summary DGME procedure with no administrative appeal (art. 222). According to the Global Detention Project (2015 data, still on its country page), detention orders are reviewed by the Tribunal Administrativo Migratorio only if the detainee appeals, and bail or home detention are rarely used. The DGME told GDP in July 2020 that deportations continued, by land, to Nicaragua and Panama. The State Department's 2019 report says the government generally observed detention safeguards and that UNHCR monitored the migration facility. I found no source documenting how often oral hearings were actually held in 2019–2020. The rating carries the structural assessment forward and is based on thin, partly government-sourced evidence about irregular migrants; I found nothing on 2020 expulsions of lawful residents.

answers.starting_answer_concern: The Yes rests on the oral hearing in art. 209 for deportation. An independent review exists only for expulsion and refugee cases, since art. 222 bars appeals against deportation and rejection. A stricter reading of 'reviewed by the competent authority' could put deportees outside the protection. This concern applies equally on both dates.
answers.notes: The law is unchanged between the two dates and the implementation rating is carried over. Confidence is low because 2020 practice evidence on hearings is sparse and partly a government self-report.
